deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a draft passage of Riemann's natural-philosophical and teleological argument for an 'Erdseele' (Earth-soul). It continues the previous page, which set out criteria for locating the cause of observed purposiveness (Zweckmäßigkeit), and leads into the next page, a draft of the published ether-inflow speculation ('Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie': thinking as a process inside ponderable matter; a space-filling substance that streams into ponderable matter and disappears there).

The argument on this page, step by step:

(i) Individual purposiveness, i.e. deliberate, goal-directed action, is perceived in humans and animals and perhaps occurs in plants. It can only be explained by a thought-process (Denkprocess) running inside those bodies themselves.

(ii) Take away the organic purposiveness. What remains in humans and animals, and in plants according to 'F's' view, is a set of interlocking relations of generation and action. 'F' is almost certainly Fechner, whose 'Nanna' (1848) argued that plants have souls. This remaining purposiveness can only be explained by one unified thought-process in the organism. Riemann says these conclusions from 'our principles' are confirmed by inner perception.

(iii) By the same principles, the cause of organic purposiveness must be sought in a single unified thought-process in the Earth. His reasons:
- (a) The relations of generation and action in organic life on Earth do not split into separate systems; everything interlocks. So it cannot be explained by several separate thought-processes in parts of the Earth.
- (b) As far as experience reaches, there is no reason to look for the cause in a still larger whole. This is because:
  - (1) The purposiveness is closed off at the Earth. Organisms are made only for life on Earth, and the Earth's crust contains the reason for their arrangement.
  - (2) Earthly organisms are individual. Experience suggests they are not repeated on other heavenly bodies.
  - (3) They do not stay the same over the Earth's life; ever new and more perfect organisms appear.
- Hence the cause lies in a simultaneous thought-process advancing to higher stages.

(iv) Conclusion: from the standpoint of exact natural science (explaining nature from causes), assuming an Earth-soul is a hypothesis to explain the existence and the historical development of the organic world. The sentence finishes on folio 18v.

The argument applies the criteria from the previous page, in parallel form. The criteria were:
- the purposive system is closed (abgeschlossen) within a body;
- it does not split into self-contained parts;
- there is no reason to refer it to a larger whole;
- non-repetition (the previous page's argument that repeated processes point to a common cause), applied in reverse;
- the presence or absence of progressive development, which decides whether the thought-process is simultaneous.

There are no derivations or formulas to restate in modern notation.
errors: No mathematical content, so no mathematical errors.

Logically, the inference from 'interlocking purposive relations' to 'a single thinking subject (Earth-soul)' is a Fechnerian analogical argument, not a demonstration. Riemann himself frames it explicitly as a hypothesis.
Point (b)(2), that organisms are not repeated on other heavenly bodies, rests on an absence of evidence, as Riemann's own inserted qualifier ('allein, was die Erfahrung darbietet') acknowledges.

results.what: Teleological argument that organic purposiveness on Earth must be explained by a unified, progressively developing thought-process of the Earth (Erdseele), a hypothesis for the existence and historical development of the organic world.
results.modern_name: Fechnerian panpsychism / Earth-soul hypothesis (natural philosophy, not mathematics)

results.what: Criteria for locating the cause of purposiveness: closure of the purposive system, non-decomposability, absence of reference to a larger whole, and progressive development implying a simultaneous thought-process.
results.modern_name: Riemann's philosophical fragments 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' (published in the Gesammelte Werke, 1876)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous publication by Weber/Dedekind), drawing on Herbart and Fechner

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's known philosophical fragments, edited by Weber/Dedekind as 'Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' in the Gesammelte Werke. His Fechner-inspired Earth-soul reasoning is documented in the literature. The draft adds only variant wording and deletions, which are of minor textual interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the deleted/inserted words before 'wahrnehmen' are most likely 'wir wahrnehmen' (Riemann corrected the verb form). The sense is 'welche wir bei Menschen und Thieren wahrnehmen'.
Line 3: 'in ihnen vorlaufenden' should read 'in ihnen verlaufenden Denkprocesse'.
'nach F's Ansicht': F = Fechner (cf. Nanna oder über das Seelenleben der Pflanzen).

Second paragraph: the struck word before 'Zeugungs- und Wirkungsbezüge' appears to be 'veränderlicher' or a similar adjective; also 'ein System ... in einander greifender ... Bezüge übrig' rather than an empty gap.

Insertion above 'Zweckmäßigkeiten' in the second paragraph is '(organischen)'. The phrase reads roughly 'welche nach Abzug dieser (organischen) Zweckmäßigkeiten bei den Menschen und Thieren [übrig bleibt]'.
'(soweit[?] (außer))' is uncertain; the sense is that the Earth's crust contains the (complete) reason for the arrangement of organisms.
Point 3: probably 'Sie bleiben nicht [dieselben] während des Lebens der Erde', with a comma and insertion mark after 'nicht'.
Last line: 'Erdseele, die eine Hypothese ...'. The 'die' is struck, and the sentence continues on 18v with 'geschichtliche Entwicklung der organischen Welt'.
Folio number '18' appears at the right margin; a marginal mark at the left edge is not transcribed.
